ut_salt_lake_slips.blurb: A compact quartzite crag on the left side of Big Cottonwood Canyon, a few miles up from the canyon mouth in the central Wasatch. About two dozen routes are described here, roughly two thirds bolted sport lines and the rest trad. Grades start at easy fifth class and top out in the 5.10 range, with most of the climbing in the moderate middle. Harder sport lines gather in a short steep cave on the left, while gentler bolted routes lie further right. Reaching the base means a hillside walk and a descent down a gully above the wall. Rattlesnakes have been reported, so watch your footing on the way in.

ut_penitentiary_wall.blurb: Penitentiary Wall is a trad-oriented quartzite wall on Big Cottonwood Canyon's southern flank, uphill from the Ledgemere picnic site. The face looks north and the routes are spread along it for about a hundred yards, most of them following obvious cracks. Nearly all of the twenty climbs are placed gear routes, with a pair that can also be top-roped. Grades cluster in the 5.7 to 5.10 range, with a few harder lines above that, and the easier cracks are well protected for their grade. Summer is the comfortable time to visit. Anchors at the top may be worn, so bring spare webbing.

ut_ledgemere_logs.blurb: A small, shady crag in Big Cottonwood Canyon near the Ledgemere picnic ground, close enough to the road and stream that traffic noise carries in. About twenty routes are spread over a few separate rocks: mostly bolted sport lines, a handful of trad climbs and a few low-grade boulder problems. The grades lean easy and friendly, with plenty of climbing from the 5.4 to 5.9 range, which makes it a good stop for newer leaders and mixed groups. The rock is the quartzite typical of the canyon, hard and a little slick, with holds at all angles. Walk-ins are short, coming either along the river or from the Dogwood side.

ut_sea_wall.blurb: Sea Wall is a limestone cliff band at the mouth of Blacksmith Fork Canyon, in Cache Valley near Hyrum. All of its twenty-odd routes are bolted sport climbs, and the density of easy and moderate lines is unusual for a crag of this size. Grades run from 5.4 up through the 5.12 range, with the largest group sitting in the 5.8 to 5.11 span, so there is something for beginners and for those pushing harder. The area is still being developed and the rock can be loose in places; wear a helmet and keep out from under other parties. The walk from the canyon mouth is short.

ut_utah_wall.blurb: One of the larger and more popular crags in Ogden Canyon, Utah Wall sits on the south side of the road a short distance above the waterfall. The cliffs here are slabby and just short of vertical. It is mainly a trad wall, with seventeen of its twenty routes protected by placed gear and a few bolted lines mixed in. Grades range from about 5.4 to the 5.10 range, centred on 5.6 to 5.8, so it suits moderate leaders and climbers building trad experience. The approach goes up a steep gully with loose rock and deserves as much care as the climbing itself. A smaller upper wall sits just above.

ut_echo_to_henefer_ice.blurb: A scattering of seasonal ice flows in and around Echo Canyon near Henefer, in the Wasatch Back, with the interstate and rail line never far away. About twenty climbs are described, mostly water ice from WI2 to WI4, with a couple of WI5 lines. Well-known flows include the Screamers and Tombstone Falls. Ice here is fickle: it comes in best after a run of big storms followed by clear, cold nights, and some winters it barely forms. Some flows are a short stroll from the road, so conditions are worth checking just before you drive out.
